# Detecting Lookahead Bias in LLM Forecasts

arXiv [2512.23847](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23847) · v1 2025-12-29 · latest 2026-06-12

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Develop a statistical test to detect lookahead bias (memorization of realized outcomes) in LLM-generated economic forecasts. | “We develop a statistical procedure to detect lookahead bias in economic forecasts generated by large language models (LLMs).” |
| **architecture** | Date-only recall query (firm name, ticker, date) yields first-token probabilities P(up), P(down), P(unknown); LAP = P(up)+P(down). The forecast signal is interacted with LAP in an accuracy regression, and a positive interaction indicates contamination. | “Augmenting the regression with the LAP main effect and the interaction \hat{\mu}\times\text{LAP}^{P(\text{known})} does.” |
| **data** | CRSP daily returns for NYSE/NASDAQ/AMEX common stocks; Compustat; Bloomberg News headlines (91,357 headlines, 1,587 firms); Thomson Reuters StreetEvents earnings call transcripts (106,994 firm-quarters, 3,920 firms). | “The in-sample dataset spans January 2012 to December 2023 and consists of 91,357 news headlines covering 1,587 unique companies. We also collect a calendar-year 2024 sample of 7,568 headlines for the post-cutoff out-of-sample placebo.” |
| **window** | Stock news: in-sample Jan 2012–Dec 2023, out-of-sample 2024. Earnings calls: in-sample 2006Q1–2020Q4, out-of-sample 2023Q3–2024Q1 (recall quarters 2024Q1–2024Q3). The split is Llama-3.3-70B's December 2023 cutoff. | “The in-sample window (2006Q1–2020Q4) yields 106,994 matched firm-quarter observations from 3,920 unique U.S. publicly listed firms. We also collect 6,744 matched firm-quarters from 2023Q3 through 2024Q1 for the post-cutoff out-of-sample placebo.” |
| **models** | Llama-3.3-70B (Meta, open-source), training cutoff December 2023, run locally with vLLM at temperature 0. | “Our analysis adopts Llama-3.3-70B, an open-source model released by Meta. Llama-3.3-70B has a publicly documented training-data knowledge cutoff of December 2023” |
| **baselines** | LLM-only regressions replicating Lopez-Lira and Tang (2023) and Jha et al. (2024); horse race against the inner-confidence measure of Chen et al. (2024). | “A horse race against the inner-confidence measure of Chen et al. (2024) shows that LAP and inner confidence load on distinct components of LLM forecasting performance.” |
| **headline_result** | Stock news in-sample: LLM×LAP interaction 0.162 (t=3.64); a one-SD increase in LAP raises the LLM marginal effect by 0.067 pp (about 32%). Capex: interaction 0.512 (t=2.01), about 12%. Both interactions are insignificant post-cutoff. | “The interaction coefficient is positive and highly significant: \hat{\delta}=0.162 ( t=3.64 ).” |
| **costs** | *not found in the text provided* | |
| **uncertainty** | t-statistics with standard errors clustered by date (news) or by firm (capex); firm/date fixed effects. Variability from batched GPU inference was verified to be negligible. | “All specifications include firm and date fixed effects, with standard errors clustered by date.” |
| **leakage_controls** | The study's purpose is to detect lookahead bias. It uses a post-training-cutoff placebo (2024) in which LAP collapses and the interaction becomes insignificant, plus an outcome-blind recall query. | “To validate that the in-sample \text{LLM}\times\text{LAP} amplification is driven by memorization rather than some other source of co-movement, we re-estimate the headline regressions on the out-of-sample window.” |
| **limitations** | The test identifies only the sign of contamination, not its magnitude. It relies on maintained assumptions, including monotonicity of the conditional slope and the exclusion of γ=1. | “Proposition 1 delivers a qualitative, one-sided test: it identifies the sign of the scalar contamination loading \gamma , not its magnitude. We do not point-estimate \gamma” |
